desc: Ideation: model as shortest paths over N^2 pair-states with recurrence dist[a][b] <= dist[l][r] + 2 for same-label edges a->l, r->b; base cases 0 (diagonal) and 1 (edges).

Write the complete Python solution: parse input, build label-bucketed incoming/outgoing edge lists, initialize dist with diagonal 0 and edges 1, run Dijkstra over pair-states (l, r) relaxing (a, b) to d+2 for matching labels a->l and r->b, then output the matrix with INF converted to -1.

Verify correctness reasoning: induction on popped distance; every palindrome walk is empty, a single edge, or matching outer letters around a shorter palindrome walk; each pair-state finalized once. Confirmed: transitions always add +2 from a strictly smaller layer, so Dial-bucket processing in increasing d guarantees first assignment is the true shortest; completeness follows since any palindrome of length ≥ 2 is c + palindrome + c. Hand-traced Sample 1 (dist[1][3]=2 via bb from (2,2), then dist[1][4]=4 via a-edges; dist[3][1]=3) and Sample 2 (dist[4][2]=3 via "sus" through state (4,1)) — both match expected outputs.

Sanity-check output format (space-separated rows, -1 for unreachable) and edge cases: N=1 with no edges prints "0"; self-loops correctly keep dist[v][v]=0 since the diagonal bit is pre-assigned; unreachable pairs remain -1; bucket list growth bounded by max distance ≤ 2·N² (~20000), memory fine; complexity O(N³) bigint ops worst case, fast for N=100.
